findings.text: System register trap triage decides among local emulation, forwarding to nested hypervisor, and fault injection. It derives the accessed encoding and direction from the trapped syndrome, looks up trap configuration, enforces feature-forbid traps, bypasses nesting work when nesting is off or when in host context outside host EL0, evaluates fine grained trap state, evaluates coarse behaviour, then either returns an index for local handling or injects into the nested guest.

Triage follows stages: unknown encoding goes local; feature-forbid bit set causes undefined injection; non-nesting or host non-EL0 goes local; fine trap bit set causes nested injection; otherwise coarse behaviour decides, with host EL0 requiring an explicit host-forward marker and read versus write requiring matching forward markers; local path handles ID space and unsupported encodings.

Fine trap register selection depends on access direction and group. Plain and debug and second-generation groups choose a read trap register for reads and a write trap register for writes, while architected-feature and instruction-trap groups use a single register. Instruction trap group additionally disables itself when a nested HCRX control indicates non-trapping of XS controls.

Fine trap evaluation never traps for host context. For positive polarity the configured bit must be set in the control register. For negative polarity a set bit means no trap; a clear bit traps only when the same bit is not marked as reserved-zero for the VM, tying trapping to whether the associated feature is implemented.

Coarse trap behaviour starts as handle-locally and accumulates additional markers. A single control identifier consults one trap-bit entry by comparing masked register value against expected value. A multi-control identifier recursively accumulates each member until a terminator. A complex identifier dispatches through a callback table indexed after the complex base.

System encoding successor increments the least significant field that has not reached its architectural mask, resetting less significant fields, in order from second opcode through control registers and first opcode to zeroth opcode. FGT mask helper bundles a symbolic name with reserved-zero and reserved-one values for a named control.

A nested trap table associates a family of GICv5 control operations with the interrupt-controller instruction trap group and zero extra control, covering enable, disable, priority, affinity, pending, configuration, hold, end-of-interrupt, deactivate and redistributor deactivate variants.

A small static table supplies default trap polarity for selected instructions outside the main range, marking synchronization, supervisor calls and return as trapping while marking one guarded-stack access as non-trapping, split across two instruction trap registers.

Nested synchronous injection is a thin wrapper that forwards a caller-supplied syndrome as a synchronous exception into the nested guest. Nested SEA injection records the fault address, builds an external-abort data or instruction syndrome with length marker, and routes to asynchronous error injection when the nested EASE control is set, otherwise to synchronous injection.

Fault injection distinguishes execution states. For 64-bit guests undefined injection builds an unknown-reason syndrome with length marker and injects synchronously; for 32-bit guests it pends an architecture-specific undefined exception. Synchronous injection pends an EL1 or EL2 synchronous exception based on target level and then records the supplied syndrome in the target exception register.

Syndrome decoding extracts operation and control fields plus direction from fixed bit positions of the trapped syndrome. ID feature space is defined as zeroth operation equal three with first operation in a restricted set and with control register zero and control modifier below a threshold.

Unsupported access logging formats operation and control fields together with read versus write kind and a caller message using variable arguments and an unimplemented-feature logger, intended so the line can be pasted as a new table entry.

Generic trap forwarding only acts in nested context when a selected control bit is set in a selected system register; on success it re-injects the current syndrome into the nested guest and reports handled. SMC forwarding tests one HCR control; debug exception forwarding tests one MDCR control.

Illegal return checking rejects returns to EL3, to an architecturally impossible mode encoding, to any 32-bit state, and to EL1 while the nested TGE control demands EL2-only operation. On illegality it preserves only interrupt masks and condition flags plus optionally PAN, NMI, PM and EXLOCK depending on implemented features, preserves exception level and width from current state, and sets the illegal-state marker.

Nested ERET emulation validates saved status, authenticates authenticated-return variants, handles pointer-authentication failure combined with FPAC support by injecting a pointer-auth exception when no illegal-state marker is already set, then performs an unload and reload around updating program counter and status under a nested-ERET marker, and finally notifies PMU state on transition.

Authenticated return selects instruction key B for B-variant and key A otherwise, bypassing authentication when the corresponding SCTLR enable is clear. It authenticates using a mask derived from address width and tagging, canonicalizes the pointer, compares computed authentication code under the mask, strips the code on success, and on failure corrupts the address either by inserting an error code or by mixing the computed code depending on PAuth version.

Code computation uses EL2 stack pointer as modifier, reading the in-memory copy when system registers are not loaded on CPU and the live stack register otherwise. It temporarily installs the guest instruction key into the generic key slot around one generic authentication instruction with barriers, then restores the host generic key.

Effective tagging for instruction authentication accounts for TBID. Without E2H it uses the single TBI and TBID controls; with E2H it selects upper or lower controls according to address bit 55. Tagging is effective only when TBI is set and TBID is clear. The lowest authenticated bit is derived from the applicable translation size clamped to a fixed minimum and maximum, and the mask covers that bit through bit 54 plus high bits when tagging is ineffective.

Canonicalization sets masked bits for high addresses and clears them for low addresses. Corruption without tagging uses a high two-bit field and with tagging uses a lower two-bit field, encoding distinct values for B-variant versus A-variant failures.
SVE user-copy region descriptor holds kernel offset, kernel length, and extra trailing user padding, describing how one slice of vector state maps between kernel and user layouts.

SVE register identifier splits a sub-identifier into a five-bit slice at shift zero and a five-bit register class above it, with masks covering each field, thirty-two slices total, and separate size constants for Z and P register encodings.

VM statistics expose only generic VM counters while vCPU statistics add counters for HVC exits, WFE and WFI exits, user and kernel MMIO exits, signal exits and total exits. Each header records name size, descriptor count, and byte offsets for identifiers, descriptors and data following the header and name area.

On this architecture the legacy get and set operations for general registers, special registers and floating point state, plus address translation, are unsupported and always report an invalid argument.

Guest debug control validates against a valid mask, clears debug state and pending single-step when enable is clear, otherwise stores the control word and copies architecture breakpoint and watchpoint state only when hardware-assisted debugging is requested.
Exit dispatch uses a function pointer type taking a vCPU and returning an integer status, with one handler per exit reason.

HVC exit handling traces the exit, counts it, and when nesting is present either injects undefined if the nested HCD control forbids HVC or forwards the trapped syndrome into the nested hypervisor; without nesting it delegates to the SMCCC handler.
Exit handling translation unit enables trace point generation for its declared trace events.

Nested ERET transition disables preemption while marking nested-ERET, unloading the vCPU, updating program counter and status, reloading on the current CPU, and clearing the marker, preventing migration or preemption across the unload and reload pair.

Pointer authentication code computation disables preemption across reading host generic keys, installing the guest key, executing barriers and the authentication instruction, and restoring the host key, protecting per-CPU key state.
An unrecognized fine-trap group indicates corrupt configuration; the code warns once with encoding and configuration and falls back to local handling rather than forwarding.

Unknown local encodings in ID space are re-injected as synchronous faults when the IDS feature is implemented and as undefined otherwise; other unknown encodings log an unimplemented-access message except for the implementation-defined range and then inject undefined.
